target_customer: Entertainment industry executives, agents, creators and fans who pay for insider Hollywood news; also sponsors and event attendees
problem: Trade press is seen as too deferential; the Ankler offers sharper, subscription funded insider reporting on the industry.
business_model: Paid newsletter subscriptions plus events, sponsorships, podcasts and a radio partnership

founders.name: Richard Rushfield
founders.background_notes: Wikipedia says he founded The Ankler in February 2017 and moved it to Substack two years later. A search snippet of a profile lists earlier DIY media projects, not verified from an opened page.

founders.name: Janice Min
founders.background_notes: Joined in January 2022 to form Ankler Media, per Wikipedia; YC lists her as a founder.

competitors.name: Puck
competitors.what: Membership based insider media startup with Hollywood newsletter What I'm Hearing led by Matthew Belloni
competitors.funding_then: $7 million at launch per TheWrap headline (2021)

technical_complexity.rationale: A newsletter on Substack with subscriptions needs little engineering; the work is editorial.

defensibility.rationale: Sources, voice and audience trust are hard to copy, but newsletter tooling is open and rivals like Puck launched in 2021.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source seen on incumbents copying or buying the Ankler; The Ankler stayed independent, with a 2024 radio deal with LAist and a move off Substack in April 2026.

market_need_then: TheWrap (June 2022) reported about 22,000 total subscriptions with paid subscriptions up 92 percent after Janice Min joined, and a profitable run of over a year per Min.

branding.domain_note: theankler.com with the article in the domain (date not found)

identity.logo: Black and white wordmark with an animated A
identity.voice_and_tone: Skeptical and direct: 'The industry, unspun' and 'The Full Story. No Spin.'

branding.brand_signature: 'The industry, unspun' voice and the insider newsletter reputation
branding.community_and_virality: Vanity Fair profile (February 2023 per YC page), Press Gazette and Axios coverage, live events and podcasts.

brand_strength.rationale: Distinctive name with an established voice, covered by trade and national press, but the name's origin is unexplained and no merch or fan community was found.

outcome_analysis: The Ankler is a profitable, independent media company by its own account. Rushfield built the newsletter from 2017, Min joined in January 2022 with Hollywood Reporter and Billboard credentials, and paid subscriptions rose 92 percent. It raised a $1.5M seed through YC in June 2022 and expanded into events, podcasts and radio. Main risks are dependence on a few journalists and competition from Puck and the trades.
notes: Seed reported by TheWrap and Wikipedia as $1.5M at a $20M valuation; the valuation is not stated as pre or post so post_money is left null. One report quotes Min saying $1.3M; aggregators say $2M or $2.03M total, unverified. Axios was blocked (403) and was not worked around. YC lists two founders with a team size of 2. Founded year 2017 is the newsletter; Ankler Media was formed around December 2021 to January 2022 and YC says 2022. Puck's entry cites an Axios URL seen in search results (not opened) and TheWrap's funding headline from a snippet. The Rushfield early projects (a college paper, an email newsletter, a fanzine) came from a search snippet only. The 2026 move to WordPress is a platform change, not a pivot.
